name: Tenable Nessus
author: Netlens
description: Shows what a Tenable Nessus scanner (Nessus Professional, Expert or Essentials) found on your devices: every finding with its severity, CVE numbers, score, whether it is known to be exploited, the port and the solution. Netlens matches each finding to a device by MAC or address, warns about new critical vulnerabilities and lists the devices at risk. Read-only: it only reads scan results, it never starts a scan.

info.title: Make an API key for Netlens
info.text: In Nessus open your user (top right) > My Account > API Keys > Generate. Copy the access key and the secret key (the secret is shown once). The keys act as that user, so use a user that can see the scans you want Netlens to read. Nessus runs on port 8834 with a certificate of its own: fill in its SHA-256 fingerprint (the browser shows it under the certificate details) and Netlens trusts exactly that certificate. Written from the Nessus API documentation and not yet tested against a real Nessus: please use Run diagnostic on the plugin's page and send the report if something looks wrong.

columns.label: Certificate fingerprint
columns.help: SHA-256 fingerprint of Nessus' certificate. When filled in, exactly that certificate is trusted; when empty the certificate is checked the normal way (see 'Verify TLS certificate').

config.label: Ignore scans older than (days)
config.help: Findings from a scan that ended longer ago are left out, so a host that was fixed and not scanned again does not stay red for ever.

config.label: Looks at the details of this many vulnerabilities
config.help: The scan lists a vulnerability by name and severity; CVE numbers, the score, 'known to be exploited' and the solution come from one extra request per vulnerability. The most serious are looked up first.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Only used for a server without a fingerprint. Nessus uses a self-signed certificate by default, so this is off by default.
